The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- #15 T12: Site preview\n- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- #20 T17: Chart builder\n- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"c08e4d08-6ab1-465b-8f44-174c4afd495a","timestamp":"2026-10-01T00:10:59.811Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.\n  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.\n  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.\n  - **Attribute values:**\n    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.\n    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.\n    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.\n    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.\n  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.\n  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Tab A's save is refused, and tab B's title and slug survive. A save with `body_dirty=0` stores the old body even when the posted HTML differs.\n- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview, at every page depth.\n  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n  - **Reuse:** delete the Report a link points to, create a new Report (which may take the old id), and the link is still plain text and marked \"Item deleted\", never a link to the new Report.\n  - Refs are backfilled for existing rows, unique, and unchanged by editing the title or slug.\n  - A new item's ref never equals a ref in `deleted_refs`. {"parentUuid":"cc612de1-e403-426f-93b5-ff1d431536f6","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"769925d1-7da0-40a1-b580-73f3237febf4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TXQHwnuAFeEvkA9uwMT7p5","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Markdown to safe HTML: the one pipeline every rendering of user-written\nMarkdown goes through: the public site, its export, and the Site preview.\n\nmarkdown-it-py renders (raw HTML in the Markdown is let through to it), then\nnh3 sanitizes, dropping <script>, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs,\nand anything else not on its allowlist. The stored body stays raw; only this\nfunction's output is ever marked safe.\n\nTwo additions to nh3's allowlist, both for Markdown tables:\n  - `style` on a table cell, but only as exactly `text-align:left|right|center`,\n    so a column's alignment (`|---:|`) survives and nothing else does.\n  - the class TABLE_SCROLL on a <div>: each Markdown table is wrapped in one, so\n    a wide table can scroll sideways without restyling the <table> itself.\n\nAnd the link rule (spec #14, \"Links\"): every site-owned link and asset is\nrelative, and only an explicit external link may be absolute. It holds for\nevery body, however it was saved, raw HTML in it included:\n  - an <a> keeps its href only if it is `https:` or `mailto:`, or a site\n    link (`report:<ref>`, `data-bite:<ref>`, app.site_links) that the\n    caller's `link_href` resolves, to where the page being rendered finds its\n    target. Any other <a> is its text.\n  - an <img> is kept only for a chart image (ADR-004), `image:<name>`, whose\n    URL the caller's `image_src` gives: it knows the item's images and where\n    the page finds them. Any other image, or a name it doesn't know, renders\n    nothing.\nnh3 checks a URL's scheme before its attribute filter sees it, so it lets\nthese schemes through, and the filter decides. An <a> or <img> the filter\nleft with no href or src is then taken out (_Unlinked).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\nfrom markdown_it.token import Token\nfrom markupsafe import Markup\n\nfrom app.site_links import TABLES as SITE_LINK_SCHEMES\n\nTABLE_SCROLL = \"content-table-scroll\"\nIMAGE_REFERENCE = \"image:\"\n# The only absolute links a body may have (spec #14, \"Links\").\nLINK_SCHEMES = (\"https:\", \"mailto:\")\n# A chart image's name -> its URL from the page being rendered; None if the\n# item has no image of that name.\nImageSrc = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n# A link's href, if it is not `https:` or `mailto:` -> the href the page\n# being rendered links by; None if it is not a site link that resolves.\nLinkHref = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n# Every scheme the link rule decides on; nh3 drops any other before it can.\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"https\", \"mailto\", \"image\", *SITE_LINK_SCHEMES}\n\n_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n\n\ndef _chart_image_name(src: str | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The name in an `image:<name>` src; None for any other.\"\"\"\n    return src.removeprefix(IMAGE_REFERENCE) if str(src).startswith(IMAGE_REFERENCE) else None\n\n_TABLE_CELLS = (\"th\", \"td\")\n_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {**nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n                       **{cell: nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.get(cell, set()) | {\"style\"}\n                          for cell in _TABLE_CELLS}}\n_TEXT_ALIGN = re.compile(r\"\\s*text-align\\s*:\\s*(left|right|center)\\s*\", re.I)\n\n\ndef table_cell_alignment(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Keep a table cell's `style` only as its text-align, and only if that is\n    one of the three a Markdown table writes; drop every other declaration.\"\"\"\n    if attribute != \"style\":\n        return value\n    if tag not in _TABLE_CELLS:\n        return None\n    for declaration in value.split(\";\"):\n        if match := _TEXT_ALIGN.fullmatch(declaration):\n            return f\"text-align:{match.group(1).lower()}\"\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_rule(image_src: ImageSrc | None, link_href: LinkHref | None):\n    \"\"\"nh3's attribute filter: the link rule, and table_cell_alignment.\"\"\"\n    def keep(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        if tag == \"a\" and attribute == \"href\":\n            if value.lower().startswith(LINK_SCHEMES):\n                return value\n            return link_href(value) if link_href else None\n        if tag == \"img\" and attribute == \"src\":\n            name = _chart_image_name(value)\n            return image_src(name) if name is not None and image_src else None\n        return table_cell_alignment(tag, attribute, value)\n\n    return keep\n\n\nclass _Unlinked(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"nh3's output as it is, less each <a> with no href (its content stays)\n    and each <img> with no src: those the link rule took them from.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=False)\n        self.out: list[str] = []\n        # Whether each open <a> is kept. nh3 never nests one in another.\n        self._anchors: list[bool] = []\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n        names = {name for name, _ in attrs}\n        if tag == \"a\":\n            self._anchors.append(\"href\" in names)\n        if (tag == \"a\" and \"href\" not in names) or (tag == \"img\" and \"src\" not in names):\n            return\n        self.out.append(self.get_starttag_text())\n\n    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):\n        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)\n        if tag == \"a\":\n            self._anchors.pop()\n\n    def handle_endtag(self, tag):\n        if tag == \"a\" and self._anchors and not self._anchors.pop():\n            return\n        self.out.append(f\"</{tag}>\")\n\n    def handle_data(self, data):\n        self.out.append(data)\n\n    def handle_entityref(self, name):\n        self.out.append(f\"&{name};\")\n\n    def handle_charref(self, name):\n        self.out.append(f\"&#{name};\")\n\n    def handle_comment(self, data):\n        self.out.append(f\"<!--{data}-->\")\n\n\ndef _unlinked(html: str) -> str:\n    parser = _Unlinked()\n    parser.feed(html)\n    parser.close()\n    return \"\".join(parser.out)\n\n\ndef render_markdown(text: str, image_src: ImageSrc | None = None,\n                    link_href: LinkHref | None = None) -> Markup:\n    \"\"\"`text` as sanitized HTML, under the link rule: its `image:<name>`\n    references resolved by `image_src`, and its site links by `link_href`.\"\"\"\n    return Markup(_unlinked(nh3.clean(_MARKDOWN.render(text or \"\"),\n                                      attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n                                      attribute_filter=_link_rule(image_src, link_href),\n                                      url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES,\n                                      allowed_classes={\"div\": {TABLE_SCROLL}})))\n\n\ndef parse(text: str) -> list[Token]:\n    \"\"\"`text`'s block tokens, parsed as render_markdown parses it.\"\"\"\n    return _MARKDOWN.parse(text or \"\")\n\n\ndef images_without_description(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The names in `text`'s `image:<name>` references that have no\n    description (alt text), in order, for the edit page to warn of: a screen\n    reader skips an image with an empty alt.\"\"\"\n    return [name for block in parse(text) for token in block.children or []\n            if token.type == \"image\" and not token.content.strip()\n            and (name := _chart_image_name(token.attrGet(\"src\"))) is not None]\n\"\"\"What Data Bites and Reports share: the title/slug/Markdown-body fields, their\nvalidation, the draft/published status, and the table-level reads and writes.\n\nEach content type keeps its own table, so a slug is unique within a type but a\nData Bite and a Report may share one (spec #1, \"Publish gate & export paths\":\nexports are namespaced by type). Who may do what is decided by each type's own\nmodule and routes, not here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom app import db, site_links\n\nSTATUS_LABELS = {\"draft\": \"Draft\", \"published\": \"Published\"}\n# Runs inside the transaction that wrote an item's row, given the connection and\n# the item's id; if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\nAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n\n\nclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    pass\n\n\nSTALE = \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\"\n\n\nclass StaleItem(ContentError):\n    \"\"\"Saved from an edit form opened on an older version of the item.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef item_base(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The version of an item an edit form was opened on: a hash of its\n    stored title, slug, and body, all three of which the form saves. A hash\n    of the body alone would let a stale form overwrite a newer title or slug.\"\"\"\n    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([title, slug, body]).encode()).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    if not title:\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n                           \"choose another.\")\n    if not body.strip():\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    return title, slug, body\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ContentTable:\n    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n    kind: str   # e.g. \"report\", its site links' scheme (app.site_links)\n\n    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n                params,\n            ).fetchall()\n\n    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n            raise exc\n        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n\n    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Create a draft, with a new ref.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                # Held from choosing the ref to storing it (site_links.new_ref).\n                conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\")\n                item_id = conn.execute(\n                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id, ref)\"\n                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, author_id, site_links.new_ref(conn)),\n                ).lastrowid\n                if also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n        return item_id\n\n    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None,\n               base: str | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. The author, created_at, and status are\n        kept. With drafts_only, a published item is left alone. With `base`,\n        the item_base the edit form was opened on, StaleItem if the item has\n        changed since, and nothing is written. False if nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                if base is not None:\n                    # Held from the check to the write, so no other save\n                    # lands between them.\n                    conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\")\n                    row = conn.execute(f\"SELECT title, slug, body FROM {self.table}\"\n                                       \" WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).fetchone()\n                    if row is not None and item_base(*row) != base:\n                        raise StaleItem(STALE)\n                changed = conn.execute(\n                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n                ).rowcount == 1\n                if changed and also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n                return changed\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n\n    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, drafts_only: bool = False,\n              also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.\n        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. With drafts_only,\n        a published item is left alone, as `update`. False if nothing was\n        changed.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            changed = conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n                (item_id, drafts_only),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n            if changed and also:\n                also(conn, item_id)\n            return changed\n\n    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n\n    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n\n    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n\n    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; None for a draft or no such item.\"\"\"\n        rows = self._select(\"c.status = 'published' AND c.slug = ?\", \"c.id\", (slug,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n                (status, item_id),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n\n    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Delete the item, leaving its ref's tombstone. False if there is no\n        such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            site_links.tombstone(conn, self.kind, item_id)\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"b55fb403-f120-481e-9b6b-42eb50092c50","timestamp":"2026-10-01T00:11:06.115Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Markdown to safe HTML: the one pipeline every rendering of user-written\nMarkdown goes through: the public site, its export, and the Site preview.\n\nmarkdown-it-py renders (raw HTML in the Markdown is let through to it), then\nnh3 sanitizes, dropping <script>, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs,\nand anything else not on its allowlist. The stored body stays raw; only this\nfunction's output is ever marked safe.\n\nTwo additions to nh3's allowlist, both for Markdown tables:\n  - `style` on a table cell, but only as exactly `text-align:left|right|center`,\n    so a column's alignment (`|---:|`) survives and nothing else does.\n  - the class TABLE_SCROLL on a <div>: each Markdown table is wrapped in one, so\n    a wide table can scroll sideways without restyling the <table> itself.\n\nAnd the link rule (spec #14, \"Links\"): every site-owned link and asset is\nrelative, and only an explicit external link may be absolute. It holds for\nevery body, however it was saved, raw HTML in it included:\n  - an <a> keeps its href only if it is `https:` or `mailto:`, or a site\n    link (`report:<ref>`, `data-bite:<ref>`, app.site_links) that the\n    caller's `link_href` resolves, to where the page being rendered finds its\n    target. Any other <a> is its text.\n  - an <img> is kept only for a chart image (ADR-004), `image:<name>`, whose\n    URL the caller's `image_src` gives: it knows the item's images and where\n    the page finds them. Any other image, or a name it doesn't know, renders\n    nothing.\nnh3 checks a URL's scheme before its attribute filter sees it, so it lets\nthese schemes through, and the filter decides. An <a> or <img> the filter\nleft with no href or src is then taken out (_Unlinked).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\nfrom markdown_it.token import Token\nfrom markupsafe import Markup\n\nfrom app.site_links import TABLES as SITE_LINK_SCHEMES\n\nTABLE_SCROLL = \"content-table-scroll\"\nIMAGE_REFERENCE = \"image:\"\n# The only absolute links a body may have (spec #14, \"Links\").\nLINK_SCHEMES = (\"https:\", \"mailto:\")\n# A chart image's name -> its URL from the page being rendered; None if the\n# item has no image of that name.\nImageSrc = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n# A link's href, if it is not `https:` or `mailto:` -> the href the page\n# being rendered links by; None if it is not a site link that resolves.\nLinkHref = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n# Every scheme the link rule decides on; nh3 drops any other before it can.\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"https\", \"mailto\", \"image\", *SITE_LINK_SCHEMES}\n\n_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n\n\ndef _chart_image_name(src: str | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The name in an `image:<name>` src; None for any other.\"\"\"\n    return src.removeprefix(IMAGE_REFERENCE) if str(src).startswith(IMAGE_REFERENCE) else None\n\n_TABLE_CELLS = (\"th\", \"td\")\n_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {**nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n                       **{cell: nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.get(cell, set()) | {\"style\"}\n                          for cell in _TABLE_CELLS}}\n_TEXT_ALIGN = re.compile(r\"\\s*text-align\\s*:\\s*(left|right|center)\\s*\", re.I)\n\n\ndef table_cell_alignment(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Keep a table cell's `style` only as its text-align, and only if that is\n    one of the three a Markdown table writes; drop every other declaration.\"\"\"\n    if attribute != \"style\":\n        return value\n    if tag not in _TABLE_CELLS:\n        return None\n    for declaration in value.split(\";\"):\n        if match := _TEXT_ALIGN.fullmatch(declaration):\n            return f\"text-align:{match.group(1).lower()}\"\n    return None\n\n\ndef _link_rule(image_src: ImageSrc | None, link_href: LinkHref | None):\n    \"\"\"nh3's attribute filter: the link rule, and table_cell_alignment.\"\"\"\n    def keep(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n        if tag == \"a\" and attribute == \"href\":\n            if value.lower().startswith(LINK_SCHEMES):\n                return value\n            return link_href(value) if link_href else None\n        if tag == \"img\" and attribute == \"src\":\n            name = _chart_image_name(value)\n            return image_src(name) if name is not None and image_src else None\n        return table_cell_alignment(tag, attribute, value)\n\n    return keep\n\n\nclass _Unlinked(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"nh3's output as it is, less each <a> with no href (its content stays)\n    and each <img> with no src: those the link rule took them from.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=False)\n        self.out: list[str] = []\n        # Whether each open <a> is kept. nh3 never nests one in another.\n        self._anchors: list[bool] = []\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n        names = {name for name, _ in attrs}\n        if tag == \"a\":\n            self._anchors.append(\"href\" in names)\n        if (tag == \"a\" and \"href\" not in names) or (tag == \"img\" and \"src\" not in names):\n            return\n        self.out.append(self.get_starttag_text())\n\n    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):\n        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)\n        if tag == \"a\":\n            self._anchors.pop()\n\n    def handle_endtag(self, tag):\n        if tag == \"a\" and self._anchors and not self._anchors.pop():\n            return\n        self.out.append(f\"</{tag}>\")\n\n    def handle_data(self, data):\n        self.out.append(data)\n\n    def handle_entityref(self, name):\n        self.out.append(f\"&{name};\")\n\n    def handle_charref(self, name):\n        self.out.append(f\"&#{name};\")\n\n    def handle_comment(self, data):\n        self.out.append(f\"<!--{data}-->\")\n\n\ndef _unlinked(html: str) -> str:\n    parser = _Unlinked()\n    parser.feed(html)\n    parser.close()\n    return \"\".join(parser.out)\n\n\ndef render_markdown(text: str, image_src: ImageSrc | None = None,\n                    link_href: LinkHref | None = None) -> Markup:\n    \"\"\"`text` as sanitized HTML, under the link rule: its `image:<name>`\n    references resolved by `image_src`, and its site links by `link_href`.\"\"\"\n    return Markup(_unlinked(nh3.clean(_MARKDOWN.render(text or \"\"),\n                                      attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n                                      attribute_filter=_link_rule(image_src, link_href),\n                                      url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES,\n                                      allowed_classes={\"div\": {TABLE_SCROLL}})))\n\n\ndef parse(text: str) -> list[Token]:\n    \"\"\"`text`'s block tokens, parsed as render_markdown parses it.\"\"\"\n    return _MARKDOWN.parse(text or \"\")\n\n\ndef images_without_description(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The names in `text`'s `image:<name>` references that have no\n    description (alt text), in order, for the edit page to warn of: a screen\n    reader skips an image with an empty alt.\"\"\"\n    return [name for block in parse(text) for token in block.children or []\n            if token.type == \"image\" and not token.content.strip()\n            and (name := _chart_image_name(token.attrGet(\"src\"))) is not None]\n\"\"\"What Data Bites and Reports share: the title/slug/Markdown-body fields, their\nvalidation, the draft/published status, and the table-level reads and writes.\n\nEach content type keeps its own table, so a slug is unique within a type but a\nData Bite and a Report may share one (spec #1, \"Publish gate & export paths\":\nexports are namespaced by type). Who may do what is decided by each type's own\nmodule and routes, not here.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom app import db, site_links\n\nSTATUS_LABELS = {\"draft\": \"Draft\", \"published\": \"Published\"}\n# Runs inside the transaction that wrote an item's row, given the connection and\n# the item's id; if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\nAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n\n\nclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    pass\n\n\nSTALE = \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\"\n\n\nclass StaleItem(ContentError):\n    \"\"\"Saved from an edit form opened on an older version of the item.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef item_base(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The version of an item an edit form was opened on: a hash of its\n    stored title, slug, and body, all three of which the form saves. A hash\n    of the body alone would let a stale form overwrite a newer title or slug.\"\"\"\n    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps([title, slug, body]).encode()).hexdigest()\n\n\ndef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    if not title:\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n                           \"choose another.\")\n    if not body.strip():\n        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    return title, slug, body\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ContentTable:\n    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n    kind: str   # e.g. \"report\", its site links' scheme (app.site_links)\n\n    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n                params,\n            ).fetchall()\n\n    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n            raise exc\n        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n\n    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Create a draft, with a new ref.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                # Held from choosing the ref to storing it (site_links.new_ref).\n                conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\")\n                item_id = conn.execute(\n                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id, ref)\"\n                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, author_id, site_links.new_ref(conn)),\n                ).lastrowid\n                if also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n        return item_id\n\n    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None,\n               base: str | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. The author, created_at, and status are\n        kept. With drafts_only, a published item is left alone. With `base`,\n        the item_base the edit form was opened on, StaleItem if the item has\n        changed since, and nothing is written. False if nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n        try:\n            with db.connect() as conn:\n                if base is not None:\n                    # Held from the check to the write, so no other save\n                    # lands between them.\n                    conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\")\n                    row = conn.execute(f\"SELECT title, slug, body FROM {self.table}\"\n                                       \" WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).fetchone()\n                    if row is not None and item_base(*row) != base:\n                        raise StaleItem(STALE)\n                changed = conn.execute(\n                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n                ).rowcount == 1\n                if changed and also:\n                    also(conn, item_id)\n                return changed\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n\n    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, drafts_only: bool = False,\n              also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.\n        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. With drafts_only,\n        a published item is left alone, as `update`. False if nothing was\n        changed.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            changed = conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n                (item_id, drafts_only),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n            if changed and also:\n                also(conn, item_id)\n            return changed\n\n    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n\n    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n\n    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n\n    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; None for a draft or no such item.\"\"\"\n        rows = self._select(\"c.status = 'published' AND c.slug = ?\", \"c.id\", (slug,))\n        return rows[0] if rows else None\n\n    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n                (status, item_id),\n            ).rowcount == 1\n\n    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Delete the item, leaving its ref's tombstone. False if there is no\n        such item.\"\"\"\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            site_links.tombstone(conn, self.kind, item_id)\n            return conn.execute(\n                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"022b05f6-d067-48fe-8235-7456f70f53a0","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":6},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"cc612de1-e403-426f-93b5-ff1d431536f6","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"9973d654-d91e-4920-9da2-a136a84a32de","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"769925d1-7da0-40a1-b580-73f3237febf4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01J17xbkRPvVsVerkk4gUV2L","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The Editor's server side (spec #14, ADR-005).\n\nThe body is stored as Markdown. The Editor shows it as HTML and posts HTML\nback, which app.markdown_form turns into Markdown again. This module decides\nwhat the Editor is shown, and what a posted body saves.\n\n**Locked blocks.** A top-level block of the stored body that the Editor can't\nrepresent (a code block, raw HTML, an inline code span, ...) is *locked*: it\nis cut out and replaced by the token `locked-<n>` (n: its place among the\nbody's locked blocks), and the Editor shows its rendered, sanitized HTML,\nread-only. Its Markdown source never reaches the browser. On save, each token\nis replaced by that block's source from the *stored* body, never from\nanything posted.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport secrets\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom urllib.parse import quote, unquote\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it.token import Token\nfrom markupsafe import Markup, escape\n\nfrom app.content import STALE, ContentError, StaleItem, item_base\nfrom app.markdown_form import LOCKED_TOKEN, ImageName, is_link, to_markdown\nfrom app.rendering import (IMAGE_REFERENCE, ImageSrc, parse, render_markdown,\n                           table_cell_alignment)\nfrom app.site_links import REFERENCE, TABLES\n\n# Block tokens the Editor can represent, and the headings among them.\n_SUPPORTED_BLOCKS = {\n    \"paragraph_open\", \"paragraph_close\", \"heading_open\", \"heading_close\", \"inline\",\n    \"bullet_list_open\", \"bullet_list_close\", \"ordered_list_open\", \"ordered_list_close\",\n    \"list_item_open\", \"list_item_close\", \"blockquote_open\", \"blockquote_close\",\n    \"table_open\", \"table_close\", \"thead_open\", \"thead_close\", \"tbody_open\", \"tbody_close\",\n    \"tr_open\", \"tr_close\", \"th_open\", \"th_close\", \"td_open\", \"td_close\",\n}\n_SUPPORTED_HEADINGS = {\"h2\", \"h3\"}\n_SUPPORTED_INLINE = {\"text\", \"softbreak\", \"hardbreak\", \"strong_open\", \"strong_close\",\n                     \"em_open\", \"em_close\", \"link_open\", \"link_close\", \"image\"}\n_NEWLINE = re.compile(r\"\\r\\n?|\\n\")\n_LAST_ENDING = re.compile(r\"(?:\\r\\n?|\\n)\\Z\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Tokenized:\n    \"\"\"A body with each locked block replaced by its token.\"\"\"\n    markdown: str\n    # 1])}\"]\n    html = str(render_markdown(\"\".join(lines), image_src, _site_link))\n    return Markup(re.sub(rf\"<p>locked-{nonce}-(\\d+)</p>\",\n                         lambda m: _locked_html(int(m[1]), locked, image_src), html))\n\n\n# What a post saves.\n\n# The Editor's HTML as nh3 lets it through, before app.markdown_form reads it:\n# only what the Editor can represent, and each locked block's token.\n_POSTED_TAGS = {\"p\", \"br\", \"strong\", \"b\", \"em\", \"i\", \"a\", \"img\", \"ul\", \"ol\", \"li\",\n                \"blockquote\", \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"table\", \"thead\",\n                \"tbody\", \"tfoot\", \"tr\", \"th\", \"td\", \"div\", \"span\"}\n_POSTED_ATTRIBUTES = {\"a\": {\"href\"}, \"img\": {\"src\", \"alt\"}, \"ol\": {\"start\"},\n                      \"th\": {\"style\", \"colspan\", \"rowspan\"},\n                      \"td\": {\"style\", \"colspan\", \"rowspan\"}, \"div\": {\"data-locked\"}}\n\n\n# A posted link's schemes, site links' included; app.markdown_form keeps\n# only the links the Editor may have (is_link).\n_POSTED_SCHEMES = {\"https\", \"mailto\", *TABLES}\n\n\ndef _sanitized(html: str) -> str:\n    return nh3.clean(html, tags=_POSTED_TAGS, attributes=_POSTED_ATTRIBUTES,\n                     attribute_filter=table_cell_alignment, link_rel=None,\n                     url_schemes=_POSTED_SCHEMES)\n\n\ndef _with_lf(text: str) -> str:\n    return _NEWLINE.sub(\"\\n\", text)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Posted:\n    \"\"\"A body as an edit form posts it. {"parentUuid":"8bf5213c-4400-47f0-a07d-de5b16077ff4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"769925d1-7da0-40a1-b580-73f3237febf4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EK4nTVggKjLi7p1To7rxC8","type":"tool_result","content":"30:def test_publish_writes_each_published_data_bite_to_its_page(client_as, tmp_path):\n41:def test_publish_writes_each_published_report_and_copies_its_file(client_as, tmp_path):\n58:def test_a_published_report_whose_stored_file_is_gone_still_publishes(client_as, tmp_path):\n69:def test_no_draft_or_draft_file_is_exported(client_as, tmp_path):\n83:def test_publishing_again_removes_what_was_unpublished(client_as, tmp_path):\n109:def test_the_export_is_the_live_public_site(client_as, client, tmp_path):\n122:def test_script_in_a_body_is_inert_in_the_export(client_as, tmp_path):\n134:def test_cms_publish_writes_site(client_as, tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):\n\"\"\"`cms publish`: write the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nThe pages and files come from app.public_site, the same ones the app serves,\nat the same paths, so the export is the live public site rather than a second\nrendering of it. That module reads only published content and links only\nrelatively, which gives the two rules the rubric checks here:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"reports/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import public_site, settings\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Regenerate `out` (site/ by default) from scratch, so a page taken down\n    since the last publish is gone from it too.\"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    # UTF-8, as the app serves them, whatever this machine's locale.\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(public_site.CSS, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for page in public_site.pages():\n        _target(out, page.path).write_text(page.render(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    for path, stored in public_site.files().items():\n        shutil.copyfile(stored, _target(out, path))\n    return out\n\n\ndef _target(out: Path, path: str) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Where `path` in the site goes under `out`, its folder made.\"\"\"\n    target = out / path\n    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return target\n\"\"\"The public site: every page a visitor can see, each described by the path\nit has in the exported site (e.g. \"data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\").\n\nThe app serves these pages at those same paths (app.routes.public), and\n`cms publish` writes them there (app.publish), so the two render one set of pages\nrather than two. Pages link to each other relatively, through `root` (\"\" at\nthe top of the site, \"../\" one folder down), so the same HTML works served\nfrom / and exported to a GitHub Pages subfolder. Where each kind of page or\nfile sits is decided here, by the *_path functions, and nowhere else.\n\nContent is read only through the published-only queries (`list_published`,\n`get_published`), so a draft cannot reach a page, a link, or the navigation.\nThe one exception is a Site preview (`data_bite_preview`, `report_preview`),\nwhich the admin console renders for one item, as if it were published, and\nwhich is never written to the site.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom types import ModuleType\n\nfrom app import data_bites, reports, settings, site_links\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* The public site's one stylesheet, at style.css in the site's root. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\n.header-home { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\n.nav-site ul { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem 1rem; list-style: none; margin: 0.5rem 0 0; padding: 0; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n/* Admin only: the message after a successful save (app.flash). */\n.admin-confirmation { background: color-mix(in srgb, #2e7d32 12%, transparent); border-left: 4px solid #2e7d32; margin: 0 0 1.5rem; padding: 0.6rem 0.9rem; }\n/* Markdown tables, in a Data Bite's or Report's body. A wide one scrolls\n   sideways in its wrapper (app.rendering.TABLE_SCROLL) rather than widening\n   the page; on a phone, rather than squeezing its text to a word a line. */\n.content-body .content-table-scroll { margin-block: 1rem; overflow-x: auto; }\n/* Chart images (app.chart_images) shrink to the column, keeping their shape. */\n.content-body img { height: auto; max-width: 100%; }\n.content-body table { border-collapse: collapse; }\n.content-body th, .content-body td { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 30%, transparent); padding: 0.35rem 0.7rem; }\n.content-body th { background: color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 8%, transparent); font-weight: 600; }\n@media (max-width: 40rem) { .content-body th, .content-body td { min-width: 10ch; } }\n/* A Site preview's banner (Page.render_preview); never on a published page. */\n.site-preview-banner { background: #fff4ce; border-left: 4px solid #9a6700; color: #4d3800; font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 1rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.9rem; }\n/* Admin only: an edit form's fields beside its Site preview, stacked below\n   them on a narrow screen. */\nbody:has(.admin-site-preview) { max-width: 90rem; }\n.admin-content-fields textarea { box-sizing: border-box; width: 100%; }\n.admin-site-preview-frame { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 30%, transparent); box-sizing: border-box; display: block; height: 75vh; min-height: 24rem; width: 100%; }\n.admin-site-preview-frame[data-width=\"phone\"] { max-width: 100%; width: 390px; }\n/* Admin only: the Editor (static/editor.js), its toolbar, and the parts of a\n   body it can't edit, shown read-only. */\n.admin-editor-label { font-weight: 600; margin: 0 0 0.25rem; }\n.admin-editor-toolbar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }\n/* The table controls, shown while the cursor is in a table. {"parentUuid":"58d7a8a8-5e26-43aa-b22c-fa082238092c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"769925d1-7da0-40a1-b580-73f3237febf4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SSRvKGdhb7nbaESCYmDzFT","type":"tool_result","content":"app/markdown_form.py:127:# A column is right-aligned when every body cell in it that isn't missing is\napp/markdown_form.py:129:_MISSING = {\"\", \"—\", \"n/a\"}\napp/markdown_form.py:131:_NUMBER = re.compile(rf\"[-+]?\\$?{_DIGITS}%?|\\(\\$?{_DIGITS}%?\\)\")\napp/markdown_form.py:262:             if cell is not None and (text := _text(cell)).lower() not in _MISSING]\napp/markdown_form.py:263:    return \"--:\" if texts and all(_NUMBER.fullmatch(text) for text in texts) else \":--\"\n# Data Bites and Reports carry chart images, referenced from the Markdown body\n\n**Status:** accepted (reverses the original spec's \"uploads for Data Bites\" exclusion, #1; spec #11)\n\nThe office's content is mostly numbers, and it already makes charts of them\nin Excel, R, and Tableau. The original spec kept Data Bites Markdown-only and\ngave Reports one attached PDF, so a chart had nowhere to go except an image\nlink to some other host. That puts it outside the draft/publish gate, and it\nbreaks when the other host changes.\n\nWe decided: **both** Data Bites and Reports can carry chart images, uploaded on\nthe item's edit page and placed in its Markdown body as `image:<name>`.\nData Bites were included on purpose, not only Reports. A Data Bite such as\n\"Fall enrollment snapshot\" is exactly where a chart is wanted.\n\n**Uploaded files, not generated charts.** The CMS stores and shows a chart\nsomeone made elsewhere; it does not draw one from data. That keeps the stack\nunchanged (no charting or image library, `pyproject.toml` is fixed), works\nwith whatever tool the office already uses, and leaves no JavaScript on the\npublic site. Charts drawn from a data block in the Markdown were considered\nand deferred as a possible stretch. Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI) were\nrejected, because they need `<iframe>` through the sanitizer.\n\n**Raster only: PNG, JPEG, WebP. No SVG.** An SVG is a document that can carry\n`<script>` and event handlers, and serving an uploaded one from the site's own\norigin would reopen the hole the Markdown sanitizer closes. Content is checked\nby signature, the way T05 checks a PDF, because there is no decoding library.\n\n**`image:<name>`, resolved at render time.** The body never holds a path. The\nMarkdown pipeline turns `image:<name>` into the URL for the page being rendered\n(admin preview, public page, or export), so one stored body works at every\ndepth and the published HTML stays relative. An unknown name renders nothing.\n\n**An image belongs to its item.** It is public only while that item is\npublished, and it follows that item's permissions (ADR-003 unchanged): any\nAnalyst may manage a Data Bite's images or a draft Report's, and only the\nDirector a published Report's. Deleting the item deletes its images.\n\nOne consequence, accepted: an image is public for as long as its item is\npublished, whether or not the body places it. An image uploaded to a\npublished Data Bite is served, and exported by `cms publish`, at once, even\nbefore the body references it. A chart that isn't ready to be seen goes on a\ndraft, not on a published item.\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\nADR-002-stack.md\nADR-003-split-publish-rights.md\nADR-004-chart-images.md\nADR-005-editor-stores-markdown.md","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"0bad373a-efed-4b5e-b968-f7e2692556dd","timestamp":"2026-10-01T00:18:49.479Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"app/markdown_form.py:127:# A column is right-aligned when every body cell in it that isn't missing is\napp/markdown_form.py:129:_MISSING = {\"\", \"—\", \"n/a\"}\napp/markdown_form.py:131:_NUMBER = re.compile(rf\"[-+]?\\$?{_DIGITS}%?|\\(\\$?{_DIGITS}%?\\)\")\napp/markdown_form.py:262:             if cell is not None and (text := _text(cell)).lower() not in _MISSING]\napp/markdown_form.py:263:    return \"--:\" if texts and all(_NUMBER.fullmatch(text) for text in texts) else \":--\"\n# Data Bites and Reports carry chart images, referenced from the Markdown body\n\n**Status:** accepted (reverses the original spec's \"uploads for Data Bites\" exclusion, #1; spec #11)\n\nThe office's content is mostly numbers, and it already makes charts of them\nin Excel, R, and Tableau. {"parentUuid":"8c47bdb3-02a2-4d01-b223-df4a4f03a115","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaZKQVbYkGAwbQVisNas","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T16 (Chart rendering, #19) is the next ticket. It has more than five parts, so here's the plan for your approval before I write any code.\n\n**Where it plugs in:** every body is rendered by one function, `render_markdown` in `app/rendering.py`. The public pages, the export and the Site preview all use it, so Charts go there once. Every save path goes through `content.validate`, so that's where chart checking goes.\n\n## Plan\n\n1. **ADR-006: Charts drawn from data**, and a link to it from the **Chart** entry in `CONTEXT.md`.\n2. **`app/charts.py`, the grammar:** strict JSON parsing (no duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity` or trailing data), every key, type and limit, single-line strings normalized to NFC, the 32 KB cap, and the canonical form. Errors name the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". Direct pytest tests.\n3. **Numbers and units:** commas, `-`, `(3.2)`, `%`, `$`, a word unit after a space, and the missing and suppressed values. Any other currency is an error, and so is a unit conflict, which names its first cell. Tests for every case.\n4. **Both save paths:** a body with an invalid chart is refused with the named error, from the Editor and from the Markdown fallback. Tests on both.\n   - *Commit, then I show you 1–4 and wait for your go-ahead.*\n5. **Drawing:** the SVG for bar, horizontal bar and line charts (1 to 4 series, legend, fixed palette, zero baseline, a note when a line chart starts above zero, missing and suppressed values leave a gap). Under it come the privacy note once, the source line, and a \"Show the data\" table that keeps the original notation.\n6. **The trusted boundary** in `render_markdown`: a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` placeholder per render, replaced exactly once after nh3 or the render fails loudly. An invalid block shows \"This chart could not be shown.\" The structural allowlist test, hostile strings, the inert placeholder a writer types, and two charts on one page.\n7. **Styling** in `public_site.CSS`, plus tests that charts appear in the Site preview, on the public page and in the export.\n8. **Browser check:** I'll show you one design with screenshots at 390, 768 and 1440 px before refining it. Chrome only, unless you can run Safari.\n9. **`/code-review`:** post the findings and how each was resolved on #19, then commit `T16: … Closes #19`.\n\n## Decisions I need you to confirm\n\n- **Chart ids versus the export.** The spec wants each chart's `id` to be `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, where the nonce is a fresh random value on every render. But the existing test checks that the export is byte-for-byte the live site, and a random value would also change every chart page on every publish. My suggestion is to keep the random nonce only for the secret placeholder. The `id` would use a value made from the body's hash: still 32 hex characters, but the same on every render. The structural test still checks the id pattern.\n- **The Editor in T16 shows a Chart as a locked block.** It's drawn and read-only, and its bytes are kept. The Edit/Remove card comes in T17. If I marked it \"supported\" now, the Editor would drop it on the first edit.\n- **Canonical form is written only when a body is edited**, either a chart typed or changed in the Markdown fallback, or (from T17) a chart from the builder. An untouched body and a locked block keep their exact bytes, as T13 requires. Validation still runs on every save, so a stored chart that fails newer rules blocks saves until it's fixed.\n- **When no unit is set, it's inferred at render time and not written into the block.** A `%` in the data makes the units `%`. The T17 builder will store the Units field.\n- **A leading `+` counts as a number**, matching the table rule from T15.\n\nTwo side notes:\n- T15's seven commits haven't been pushed, so #18 is still open.
