stored_body(data_bites, item_id) == body + \"\\nMore.\\n\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"editor\", \"fallback\"])\ndef test_a_stored_chart_not_in_canonical_form_keeps_its_bytes(analyst, then /bin/sh \"${HOME-}/.orca/agent-hooks/claude-hook.sh\"; else { command -p cat 2>/dev/null || cat; } >/dev/null 2>&1 || :; printf '{}\\n'; fi ;; esac; fi","durationMs":26},"type":"attachment","uuid":"f684b5db-7495-4eb3-b945-a7b378e8abf9","timestamp":"2026-10-01T14:09:37.318Z","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"f684b5db-7495-4eb3-b945-a7b378e8abf9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"39316eac-0adf-4f6e-ae8f-cb69110b6f6f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.285/8048572d43f2c8fff17a2a36cc48dbb8/dataviz\n\n# Data Visualization\n\nA chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns \"make it look\ngood\" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather\nthan by taste.\n\n**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form\nheuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design\nsystem supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a\ndiverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);\nthe method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the\nreference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your\nbrand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.\n\n> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**\n> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.\n\n## The procedure - do these in order\n\nColor comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.\n\n1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a\n   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes\n   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`\n2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential\n   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.\n   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`\n3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**\n   `node scripts/validate_palette.js \"<hex,hex,...>\" --mode light` (relative to\n   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type=\"module\">` in the\n   chart's own page, where it reads\n   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns\n   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,\n   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for\n   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.\n4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to\n   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked\n   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,\n   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`\n5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship\n   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.\n   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger\n   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`\n6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4\n   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names\n   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own\n   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic\n   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.\n7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or\n   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow\n   before calling it done.\n\nThen check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog\nof what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.\n\n## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)\n\n- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a\n  generated hue - it folds into \"Other,\" small multiples, or composite encoding.\n- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different\n  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the\n  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*\n- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series\n  count must not repaint the survivors.\n- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray\n  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.\n- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the\n  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A\n  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the\n  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse\n  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN\n  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.\n- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with\n  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**\n- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends\n  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.\n- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused\n  for \"series 4\"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.\n\n## Plugging in a design system\n\nThe method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference\ninstance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.\n\n| Parameter | What the system provides |\n|---|---|\n| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |\n| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |\n| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |\n| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |\n| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |\n| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |\n| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |\n| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |\n\nTo onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let\nit snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.\n\n## Reference files\n\n| File | What it answers |\n|------|-----------------|\n| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |\n| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |\n| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |\n| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |\n| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |\n| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |\n| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |\n| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"e422bdcf-ae60-4095-8c24-658c51a77df9","timestamp":"2026-10-01T14:09:37.291Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01FAfixMuVVQ9NDUqCN1RkgR","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"8cd84221-be07-42e7-8eaf-d7d1333e86cc","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"39316eac-0adf-4f6e-ae8f-cb69110b6f6f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TAt2GNyiDJ9vhoftnM8mLE","type":"tool_result","content":"# Reference palette\n\nThis is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the\nmethod needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill\nis system-agnostic - **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and\nre-run the validator. Nothing else changes.\n\n## How to use these values\n\nEverything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as\nCSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then\nreference them by role throughout - so the light/dark values swap in one place,\nand the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:\n\n```css\n.viz-root {\n  color-scheme: light;\n  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */\n  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;\n  --text-secondary: #52514e;\n  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */\n  /* ...only the roles this chart uses */\n}\n@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {\n  :root:where(:not([data-theme=\"light\"])) .viz-root {\n    color-scheme: dark;\n    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;\n    --text-primary:   #ffffff;\n    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;\n    --series-1:       #3987e5;\n  }\n}\n:root[data-theme=\"dark\"] .viz-root {\n  color-scheme: dark;\n  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;\n  --text-primary:   #ffffff;\n  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;\n  --series-1:       #3987e5;\n}\n```\n\nDeclare the dark values under both scopes as above - the media query covers\nthe OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,\nwhich must win both ways (the `:not(...)` guard lets a light stamp beat\nOS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).\n\n## Categorical palette\n\nBoth modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the\ndark surface, not a separate palette:\n\n| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |\n|------|-----|-------|------|\n| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |\n| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |\n| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |\n| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |\n| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |\n| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |\n| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |\n| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |\n\nThis order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*\npairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD Delta E 9.1 light / 8.4 dark\n(OKLab ×100, >=8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision Delta E 19.6 light / 19.3\ndark (>=15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small\nmultiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors - with all 28 pairs in\nplay no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and\nre-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule - so those\nchart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs\nin both modes** (worst pair CVD Delta E 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0\nlight / 20.9 dark - clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to \"Other\" or\nfacet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen\ntogether, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7\nlight; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)\nsit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship\nvisible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the\ndark band (OKLCH L ~ 0.48-0.67, >= 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a\nset. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening -\nthe same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex\nchanges. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its\ndark run in the 6-8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;\nthis order deliberately trades that fourth slot - yellow now sits beside orange -\nfor better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow<->orange\nconfusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a\npure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full\ngate.\n\nThe slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic - candidate\norderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both\nmodes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the\npassing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in\nyour brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and\nchoose only among the passing ones.\n\n## Sequential hue\n\nDefault single hue: **blue**, light->dark. When two sequential contexts appear at\nonce, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own\none-hue ramp.\n\n| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |\n| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |\n| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |\n| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |\n\nThe full 100->700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude -\nheatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means \"near zero\" and is allowed\nto recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks -\nfunnel stages, tiers - validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface\nmust still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,\n2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).\n\n## Diverging pair\n\n**blue <-> red** - warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray\n(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue<->aqua was\nrejected - both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as \"nothing\".)\n\n## Status palette (fixed - never themed)\n\n| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |\n| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |\n| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |\n| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |\n\nDark: same four steps - all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain\ndistinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and\nserious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so\na status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct\nfrom the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series -\ndistinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to\ncarry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar\n(unsimulated Delta E >= 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit\nbelow 15 - in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure\n4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text\ngreen `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)\nholds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. Every element goes through\n_element, which refuses any element or attribute outside the spec's fixed\nvocabulary, and any attribute value that isn't one of:\n  - a number this module formatted (and checked with math.isfinite),\n  - a palette constant (fill, stroke), a fixed class name, or a fixed token,\n  - the title's id, `chart-<key>-<n>-title`.\nWriter strings (title, labels, units, source, category and series names,\ncell text) are only ever text content, escaped by _text.\n\nLayout is in the SVG's own units: the stylesheet (app.public_site.CSS) sets\nits text to FONT units and scales the SVG to the column.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom html import escape\n\nfrom app.charts import PREFIX, Chart, Unit\n\n# The palette (dataviz reference palette, slots 1 to 4, light steps). The\n# stylesheet swaps in the dark steps by class in dark mode.\nSERIES = (\"#2a78d6\", \"#eb6834\", \"#1baf7a\", \"#eda100\")\nINK = \"#52514e\"       # labels, values, legend, axis titles\nMUTED = \"#898781\"     # tick labels\nGRID = \"#e1e0d9\"\nBASELINE = \"#a3a29b\"\nSURFACE = \"#ffffff\"   # the ring around a marker\nNONE = \"none\"         # a line's fill\nPALETTE = frozenset({*SERIES, INK, MUTED, GRID, BASELINE, SURFACE, NONE})\n\nELEMENTS = frozenset({\"figure\", \"figcaption\", \"svg\", \"g\", \"title\", \"rect\", \"line\", \"polyline\",\n                      \"circle\", \"text\", \"p\", \"small\", \"details\", \"summary\", \"table\", \"thead\",\n                      \"tbody\", \"tr\", \"th\", \"td\"})\nATTRIBUTES = frozenset({\"class\", \"viewBox\", \"role\", \"aria-labelledby\", \"aria-hidden\", \"id\", \"x\",\n                        \"y\", \"x1\", \"y1\", \"x2\", \"y2\", \"width\", \"height\", \"cx\", \"cy\", \"r\",\n                        \"points\", \"fill\", \"stroke\", \"stroke-width\", \"text-anchor\", \"scope\"})\n_SERIES_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-series-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\n_LINE_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-line-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\n_MARKER_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-marker-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\nCLASSES = frozenset({\"chart-figure\", \"chart-title\", \"chart-svg\", \"chart-grid\", \"chart-baseline\",\n                     \"chart-tick\", \"chart-category\", \"chart-value\", \"chart-axis-title\",\n                     \"chart-legend\", \"chart-note\", \"chart-source\", \"chart-data\",\n                     *_SERIES_CLASSES, *_LINE_CLASSES, *_MARKER_CLASSES})\n_TOKENS = {\"role\": {\"img\"}, \"text-anchor\": {\"start\", \"middle\", \"end\"}, \"scope\": {\"row\", \"col\"},\n           \"aria-hidden\": {\"true\"}}\nTITLE_ID = re.compile(r\"chart-[0-9a-f]{32}-[0-9]+-title\")\n\nPRIVACY_NOTE = \"Some values are suppressed for privacy.\"\nDATA_SUMMARY = \"Show the data\"\n\nWIDTH = 520\nFONT = 13            # the stylesheet's size for the SVG's text\n_CHAR = FONT * 0.6   # an estimate of one character's width\n_LINE = 18           # a line of text\n_PLOT_HEIGHT = 220\n_BAR = 24            # the thickest a bar is\n_GAP = 2             # between touching bars\n\n\nclass ChartDrawError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"The drawing broke its own rules: a bug, never a writer's mistake.\"\"\"\n\n\n# Building elements.\n\ndef _number(value: float) -> str:\n    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value):\n        raise ChartDrawError(f\"not a finite number: {value!r}\")\n    text = f\"{value:.2f}\".rstrip(\"0\").rstrip(\".\")\n    return \"0\" if text == \"-0\" else text\n\n\ndef _value(name: str, value: object) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An attribute's value, if the vocabulary allows it.\"\"\"\n    if name == \"viewBox\":\n        return \" \".join(map(_number, value))\n    if name == \"points\":\n        return \" \".join(f\"{_number(x)},{_number(y)}\" for x, y in value)\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and name not in (\"id\", \"aria-labelledby\", \"class\"):\n        return _number(value)\n    allowed = (name == \"class\" and value in CLASSES\n               or name in (\"fill\", \"stroke\") and value in PALETTE\n               or name in (\"id\", \"aria-labelledby\") and TITLE_ID.fullmatch(str(value))\n               or value in _TOKENS.get(name, ()))\n    if not allowed:\n        raise ChartDrawError(f\"{name}={value!r} is not in the vocabulary\")\n    return str(value)\n\n\ndef _element(name: str, attributes: dict | None = None, *content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An element of the vocabulary. `content` is elements from here, or\n    _text: never a writer's string as it is.\"\"\"\n    if name not in ELEMENTS:\n        raise ChartDrawError(f\"<{name}> is not in the vocabulary\")\n    parts = []\n    for key, value in (attributes or {}).items():\n        if key not in ATTRIBUTES:\n            raise ChartDrawError(f\"{key} is not in the vocabulary\")\n        parts.append(f' {key}=\"{_value(key, value)}\"')\n    return f\"<{name}{''.join(parts)}>{''.join(content)}</{name}>\"\n\n\ndef _text(text: str) -> str:\n    return escape(text, quote=True)\n\n\ndef _width(text: str) -> float:\n    return len(text) * _CHAR\n\n\ndef _fit(text: str, room: float) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`text`, shortened with an ellipsis to fit `room` units.\"\"\"\n    if _width(text) <= room:\n        return text\n    keep = max(1, int(room // _CHAR) - 1)\n    return text[:keep].rstrip() + \"…\"\n\n\ndef _label(x: float, y: float, text: str, css: str, anchor: str = \"middle\",\n           fill: str = INK) -> str:\n    return _element(\"text\", {\"class\": css, \"x\": x, \"y\": y, \"text-anchor\": anchor, \"fill\": fill},\n                    _text(text))\n\n\n# Scales and ticks.\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Scale:\n    low: float\n    high: float\n    step: float\n\n    @property\n    def ticks(self) -> list[float]:\n        count = round((self.high - self.low) / self.step)\n        return [round(self.low + i * self.step, 10) for i in range(count + 1)]\n\n    def at(self, value: float, start: float, length: float) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Where `value` falls along an axis from `start`, `length` long.\"\"\"\n        return start + length * (value - self.low) / (self.high - self.low)\n\n\ndef _scale(values: Sequence[float], *, from_zero: bool) -> Scale:\n    \"\"\"A scale with round ticks over `values`. A bar chart's (`from_zero`)\n    always takes in zero; a line chart's does when its values come close.\"\"\"\n    low, high = (min(values), max(values)) if values else (0.0, 1.0)\n    if from_zero or (low > 0 and low <= high / 3):\n        low = min(low, 0.0)\n    if from_zero or (high < 0 and high >= low / 3):\n        high = max(high, 0.0)\n    span = high - low or abs(high) or 1.0\n    raw = span / 5\n    magnitude = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(raw))\n    step = next(m * magnitude for m in (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10) if m * magnitude >= raw)\n    low, high = math.floor(low / step) * step, math.ceil(high / step) * step\n    if high == low:\n        high = low + step\n    return Scale(low, high, step)\n\n\ndef _tick_text(value: float, step: float, unit: Unit | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A tick's label: a round number, with the units if they are $ or %.\"\"\"\n    decimals = max(0, -math.floor(math.log10(step) + 1e-9))\n    if round(step * 10 ** decimals, 6) % 1:\n        decimals += 1\n    digits = f\"{abs(value):,.{decimals}f}\"\n    sign = \"-\" if value < 0 and digits.strip(\"0.,\") else \"\"\n    if unit and unit.text == \"$\":\n        return f\"{sign}${digits}\"\n    if unit and unit.text == \"%\":\n        return f\"{sign}{digits}%\"\n    return sign + digits\n\n\ndef _value_title(chart: Chart) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The value axis's title: the y label, or else units that are a word.\"\"\"\n    unit = chart.effective_unit\n    if chart.y_label:\n        return chart.y_label\n    return unit.text if unit and unit.text not in (\"$\", \"%\") else None\n\n\n# The legend.\n\ndef _legend(chart: Chart, top: float) -> tuple[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"The legend for two or more series, from `top`, and its height.\"\"\"\n    if len(chart.series) < 2:\n        return \"\", 0.0\n    items, x, y = [], 0.0, top + FONT\n    for index, series in enumerate(chart.series):\n        name = _fit(series.name, WIDTH - 20)\n        width = 18 + _width(name) + 16\n        if x and x + width > WIDTH:\n            x, y = 0.0, y + _LINE\n        if chart.type == \"line\":\n            swatch = _element(\"line\", {\"class\": _LINE_CLASSES[index], \"x1\": x, \"y1\": y - 4,\n                                       \"x2\": x + 14, \"y2\": y - 4, \"stroke\": SERIES[index],\n                                       \"stroke-width\": 2})\n        else:\n            swatch = _element(\"rect\", {\"class\": _SERIES_CLASSES[index], \"x\": x, \"y\": y - 10,\n                                       \"width\": 12, \"height\": 12, \"fill\": SERIES[index]})\n        items.append(swatch + _label(x + 18, y, name, \"chart-legend\", \"start\"))\n        x += width\n    return _element(\"g\", {\"class\": \"chart-legend\"}, *items), y - top + 10\n\n\ndef _mark_title(chart: Chart, series_name: str, category: str, text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A mark's tooltip: what it is, and its value as typed.\"\"\"\n    named = f\"{series_name}, {category}\" if len(chart.series) > 1 else category\n    return _element(\"title\", None, _text(f\"{named}: {text}\"))\n\n\n# Bar and line charts: categories along the bottom.\n\ndef _category_labels(categories: Sequence[str], centre, step: float, y: float) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The categories under the plot, every k-th if they're crowded, each\n    shortened to the room it has.\"\"\"\n    least = 4 * _CHAR + 4\n    every = max(1, math.ceil(least / step)) if step < least else 1\n    room = every * step - 4\n    labels = []\n    for index, category in enumerate(categories):\n        if index % every:\n            continue\n        labels.append(_label(centre(index), y, _fit(category, room), \"chart-category\"))\n    return labels\n\n\ndef _vertical(chart: Chart) -> tuple[str, float, Scale]:\n    unit = chart.effective_unit\n    numbers = [cell.number for cell in chart.cells() if cell.kind == \"number\"]\n    scale = _scale(numbers, from_zero=chart.type == \"bar\")\n    ticks = [(tick, _tick_text(tick, scale.step, unit)) for tick in scale.ticks]\n    single = len(chart.series) == 1\n    legend, legend_height = _legend(chart, 0)\n    value_title = _value_title(chart)\n    top = legend_height + (_LINE if value_title else 0) + 10\n    left = max(_width(text) for _, text in ticks) + 10\n    end_label = \"\"\n    if chart.type == \"line\" and single:\n        last = [cell for cell in chart.series[0].cells if cell.kind == \"number\"]\n        end_label = last[-1].text if last else \"\"\n    right = 12 + (_width(end_label) + 8 if end_label else 0)\n    plot_width = WIDTH - left - right\n    bottom = top + _PLOT_HEIGHT\n\n    def y(value: float) -> float:\n        return scale.at(value, bottom, -_PLOT_HEIGHT)\n\n    parts = [legend]\n    if value_title:\n        parts.append(_label(0, legend_height + FONT, _fit(value_title, WIDTH), \"chart-axis-title\",\n                            \"start\"))\n    grid = []\n    for tick, text in ticks:\n        grid.append(_element(\"line\", {\"class\": \"chart-grid\", \"x1\": left, \"y1\": y(tick),\n                                      \"x2\": left + plot_width, \"y2\": y(tick), \"stroke\": GRID,\n = 0.0 if scale.low <= 0 <= scale.high else scale.low\n    parts.append(_element(\"line\", {\"class\": \"chart-baseline\", \"x1\": left, \"y1\": y(base),\n                                   \"x2\": left + plot_width, \"y2\": y(base), \"stroke\": BASELINE,\n                                   \"stroke-width\": 1}))\n    count = len(chart.categories)\n    if chart.type == \"bar\":\n        step = plot_width / count\n        parts.extend(_bars(chart, left, step, y))\n\n        def centre(index: int) -> float:\n            return left + (index + 0.5) * step\n    else:\n        inset = 12\n        step = (plot_width - 2 * inset) / (count - 1)\n        parts.extend(_lines(chart, lambda index: left + inset + index * step, y, end_label))\n\n        def centre(index: int) -> float:\n            return left + inset + index * step\n    labels_y = bottom + 6 + FONT\n    parts.append(_element(\"g\", None, *_category_labels(chart.categories, centre, step, labels_y)))\n    height = labels_y + 6\n    if chart.x_label:\n        height += _LINE\n        parts.append(_label(left + plot_width / 2, height - 6, _fit(chart.x_label, WIDTH),\n                            \"chart-axis-title\"))\n    return \"\".join(parts), height, scale\n\n\ndef _bars(chart: Chart, left: float, step: float, y) -> list[str]:\n    count = len(chart.series)\n    group = min(step * 0.7, count * _BAR + (count - 1) * _GAP)\n    width = (group - (count - 1) * _GAP) / count\n    single = count == 1\n    labelled = single and all(_width(cell.text) <= step - 2 for cell in chart.series[0].cells)\n    marks, labels = [], []\n points = [(x(index), y(cell.number)) if cell.kind == \"number\" else None\n                  for index, cell in enumerate(series.cells)]\n        lines, markers = [], []\n        for run in Every element goes through\n_element, which refuses any element or attribute outside the spec's fixed\nvocabulary, and any attribute value that isn't one of:\n  - a number this module formatted (and checked with math.isfinite),\n  - a palette constant (fill, stroke), a fixed class name, or a fixed token,\n  - the title's id, `chart-<key>-<n>-title`.\nWriter strings (title, labels, units, source, category and series names,\ncell text) are only ever text content, escaped by _text.\n\nLayout is in the SVG's own units: the stylesheet (app.public_site.CSS) sets\nits text to FONT units and scales the SVG to the column.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom html import escape\n\nfrom app.charts import PREFIX, Chart, Unit\n\n# The palette (dataviz reference palette, slots 1 to 4, light steps). \"fill\", \"stroke\", \"stroke-width\", \"text-anchor\", \"scope\"})\n_SERIES_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-series-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\n_LINE_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-line-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\n_MARKER_CLASSES = tuple(f\"chart-marker-{i}\" for i in range(1, len(SERIES) + 1))\nCLASSES = frozenset({\"chart-figure\", \"chart-title\", \"chart-svg\", \"chart-grid\", \"chart-baseline\",\n                     \"chart-tick\", \"chart-category\", \"chart-value\", \"chart-axis-title\",\n                     \"chart-legend\", \"chart-note\", \"chart-source\", \"col\"},\n           \"aria-hidden\": {\"true\"}}\nTITLE_ID = re.compile(r\"chart-[0-9a-f]{32}-[0-9]+-title\")\n\nPRIVACY_NOTE = \"Some values are suppressed for privacy.\"\nDATA_SUMMARY = \"Show the raise ChartDrawError(f\"not a finite number: {value!r}\")\n    text = f\"{value:.2f}\".rstrip(\"0\").rstrip(\".\")\n    return \"0\" if text == \"-0\" else text\n\n\ndef _value(name: str, value: return \" \".join(f\"{_number(x)},{_number(y)}\" for x, y in value)\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and name not in (\"id\", \"aria-labelledby\", \"class\"):\n        return _number(value)\n (low > 0 and low <= high / 3):\n        low = min(low, 0.0)\n    if from_zero or (high < 0 and high >= low / 3):\n        high = max(high, 0.0)\n    span = high - low or abs(high) or 1.0\n    raw = span / 5\n    magnitude = 10 ** math.floor(math.log10(raw))\n    step = next(m * magnitude for m in (1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10) if m * magnitude >= raw)\n    low, high = math.floor(low / step) * step, return \"\", 0.0\n    items, x, y = [], 0.0, top + FONT\n    for index, series in enumerate(chart.series):\n        name = _fit(series.name, WIDTH - 20)\n        width = 18 + _width(name) + 16\n [(tick, _tick_text(tick, scale.step, unit)) for tick in scale.ticks]\n    single = len(chart.series) == 1\n    legend, legend_height = _legend(chart, 0)\n    value_title = _value_title(chart)\n    top = legend_height + (_LINE if value_title else 0) + 10\n    left = max(_width(text) for _, text in ticks) + 10\n    end_label = \"\"\n    if chart.type == \"line\" and single:\n        last = [cell for Drawing (app.chart_drawing), the trusted\nSVG boundary in app.rendering, and Charts on the Site preview, the public\npage, and the export.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport re\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import chart_drawing, charts, rendering\nfrom app.chart_drawing import CLASSES, ELEMENTS, PALETTE, ChartDrawError\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom app.rendering import CHART_NOT_SHOWN, ChartPlacementError, render_markdown\nfrom tests.test_t07_public_site import crawl, published_bite, published_report\nfrom tests.test_t08_publish import exported\nfrom tests.test_t09_tables import content_body\nfrom tests.test_t12_site_preview import preview\nfrom tests.test_t16_charts import chart_data, fence, series\n\nATTRIBUTES = {\"class\", \"viewBox\", \"role\", \"aria-labelledby\", \"aria-hidden\", \"id\", \"x\", \"y\",\n              \"x1\", \"y1\", \"x2\", \"y2\", \"width\", \"height\", \"cx\", \"cy\", \"r\", \"points\", \"fill\",\n              \"stroke\", \"stroke-width\", \"text-anchor\", \"scope\"}\nTITLE_ID = re.compile(r\"chart-[0-9a-f]{32}-[0-9]+-title\")\n\n\nclass Figure(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"A rendered figure, as html.parser reads it: every element and\n    attribute, and every piece of text content.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, html: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)\n        self.elements: list[str] = []\n        self.attributes: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n        self.texts: list[str] = []\n        self.feed(html)\n        self.close()\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n        self.elements.append(tag)\n        self.attributes.extend((tag, name, value or \"\") for name, value in attrs)\n\n    handle_startendtag = handle_starttag\n\n    def handle_data(self, data):\n        self.texts.append(data)\n\n    def values(self, name: str) -> list[str]:\n        return [value for _, attribute, value in self.attributes if attribute == name]\n\n    def named(self, tag: str, **attributes: str) -> int:\n        \"\"\"How many `tag` elements there are (with these attribute values).\"\"\"\n        return sum(1 for _ in self._starts(tag, attributes))\n\n    def _starts(self, tag, attributes):\n        # Element starts are in order; rebuild each one's attributes.\n        index = 0\n        for element in self.elements:\n            own = []\n            while index < len(self.attributes) and self.attributes[index][0] == element and (\n                    not own or self.attributes[index][1] not in {name for name, _ in own}):\n                own.append(self.attributes[index][1:])\n                index += 1\n            if element == tag and all((name, value) in own\n                                      for name, value in attributes.items()):\n                yield own\n\n\ndef drawn(**override) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A body holding one Chart, rendered.\"\"\"\n    return str(render_markdown(fence(json.dumps(chart_data(**override)))))\n\n\ndef figure_of(**override) -> Figure:\n    html = drawn(**override)\n    assert html.startswith('<figure class=\"chart-figure\">') and html.endswith(\"</figure>\"), html\n    return Figure(html)\n\n\nALL_OPTIONAL = {\"x_label\": \"Class\", \"y_label\": \"Students\", \"source\": \"Registrar, census date\"}\nFOUR = [series(\"1,200\", \"-5\", \"\", \"<10\", name=\"A\"), series(\"$3\", \"(4)\", \"n/a\", \"*\", name=\"B\"),\n        series(\"2\", \"0\", \"—\", \"≤5\", name=\"C\"), series(\"-$1,000.5\", \"7\", \"8\", \"<=5\", name=\"D\")]\nCHARTS = [\n    *[pytest.param({\"type\": kind}, id=f\"{kind}-one-series\") for kind in charts.TYPES],\n    *[pytest.param({\"type\": kind, \"categories\": [\"A\", \"B\", \"C\", \"D\"], \"series\": FOUR,\n                    **ALL_OPTIONAL}, id=f\"{kind}-four-series-negatives-missing-suppressed\")\n      for kind in charts.TYPES],\n    pytest.param({\"type\": \"line\", \"categories\": [f\"{2000 + i}\" for i in range(60)],\n                  \"series\": [series(*[str(900 + i) for i in range(60)])],\n                  \"unit\": {\"text\": \"students\", \"position\": \"suffix\"}}, id=\"line-sixty-points\"),\n    pytest.param({\"type\": \"bar\", \"categories\": [f\"Category {i}\" for i in range(30)],\n                  \"series\": [series(*[\"12%\"] * 30)]}, id=\"bar-thirty-categories\"),\n    pytest.param({\"type\": \"hbar\", \"series\": [series(\"n/a\", \"—\")]}, id=\"hbar-all-missing\"),\n]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"override\", CHARTS)\ndef test_the_figure_uses_only_the_fixed_vocabulary(override):\n    \"\"\"The structural allowlist test (spec #14).\"\"\"\n    figure = figure_of(**override)\n    assert set(figure.elements) <= ELEMENTS\n    assert {name for _, name, _ in figure.attributes} <= ATTRIBUTES\n    for name in (\"fill\", \"stroke\"):\n        assert set(figure.values(name)) <= PALETTE, name\n    assert set(figure.values(\"class\")) <= CLASSES\n    assert all(TITLE_ID.fullmatch(value) for value in figure.values(\"id\"))\n    assert all(TITLE_ID.fullmatch(value) for value in figure.values(\"aria-labelledby\"))\n    names = {name for _, name, _ in figure.attributes}\n    assert not names & {\"href\", \"xlink:href\", \"style\", \"src\"}\n    assert not any(name.startswith(\"on\") for name in names)\n\n\ndef test_the_vocabulary_is_the_specs():\n    assert ELEMENTS == {\"figure\", \"figcaption\", \"svg\", \"g\", \"title\", \"rect\", \"line\", \"polyline\",\n                        \"circle\", \"text\", \"p\", \"small\", \"details\", \"summary\", \"table\", \"thead\",\n                        \"tbody\", \"tr\", \"th\", \"td\"}\n    assert chart_drawing.ATTRIBUTES == ATTRIBUTES\n\n\nHOSTILE = [\"<script>alert(1)</script>\", '\"><svg onload=alert(1)>', \"javascript:alert(1)\",\n           \"</title><script>x</script>\", \"Tom & Jerry &amp; <b>\"]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"hostile\", HOSTILE)\ndef test_hostile_writer_strings_are_only_escaped_text(hostile):\n    html = drawn(type=\"line\", title=hostile, x_label=hostile[:60], y_label=hostile[:60],\n                 source=hostile, unit={\"text\": hostile[:20], \"position\": \"suffix\"},\n                 categories=[hostile[:60], \"Senior\"],\n                 series=[series(\"<10\", \"≤5\", name=hostile[:40]), series(\"1\", \"2\", name=\"B\")])\n    figure = Figure(html)\n    assert set(figure.elements) <= ELEMENTS\n    assert not any(hostile[:20] in value for _, _, value in figure.attributes)\n    text = \"\".join(figure.texts)\n    assert hostile in text and hostile[:20] in text\n    assert \"<script\" not in html and \"<b>\" not in html and \"<svg onload\" not in html\n\n\ndef test_a_placeholder_typed_by_the_writer_is_inert_text():\n    typed = \"chart-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-0\"\n    html = str(render_markdown(f\"{typed}\\n\\n\" + fence(json.dumps(chart_data()))))\n    assert html.startswith(f\"<p>{typed}</p>\")\n    assert html.count(\"<figure\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_a_writer_who_somehow_typed_the_nonce_gets_a_loud_failure(monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Missing, extra, or leftover placeholders raise, never render partly.\"\"\"\n    monkeypatch.setattr(rendering.secrets, \"token_hex\", lambda n: \"f\" * 32)\n    for extra in (f\"chart-{'f' * 32}-0\", f\"chart-{'f' * 32}-1\", f\"x chart-{'f' * 32}-0 y\"):\n        with pytest.raises(ChartPlacementError):\n            render_markdown(f\"{extra}\\n\\n\" + fence(json.dumps(chart_data())))\n\n\ndef test_a_placeholder_nh3_lost_fails_loudly(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setattr(rendering.nh3, \"clean\", lambda html, **_: \"<p>gone</p>\")\n    with pytest.raises(ChartPlacementError):\n        render_markdown(fence(json.dumps(chart_data())))\n\n\ndef test_two_charts_get_distinct_placeholders_and_each_render_a_fresh_nonce(monkeypatch):\n    nonces = iter([\"a\" * 32, \"b\" * 32])\n    monkeypatch.setattr(rendering.secrets, \"token_hex\", lambda n: next(nonces))\n    body = fence(json.dumps(chart_data(title=\"One\"))) + \"\\n\" + fence(json.dumps(chart_data(title=\"Two\")))\n    env = {\"nonce\": rendering.secrets.token_hex(16), \"charts\": []}\n    html = rendering._MARKDOWN.render(body, env)\n    assert html == f\"<p>chart-{'a' * 32}-0</p>\\n<p>chart-{'a' * 32}-1</p>\\n\"\n    rendered = str(render_markdown(body))\n    assert rendered.index(\">One<\") < rendered.index(\">Two<\")\n    assert re.findall(r'id=\"(chart-[0-9a-f]{32}-\\d+-title)\"', rendered) == [\n        f\"chart-{key}-{n}-title\" for key, n in zip([rendered.split(\"chart-\")[1][:32]] * 2, (0, 1))]\n\n\ndef test_an_invalid_chart_renders_only_the_fixed_text():\n    for source in (\"{\", json.dumps(chart_data(type=\"pie\")), '{\"title\": \"<script>x</script>\"}'):\n        assert str(render_markdown(fence(source))) == f\"<p>{CHART_NOT_SHOWN}</p>\\n\"\n\n\ndef test_only_a_chart_fence_is_drawn():\n    html = str(render_markdown(\"```json\\n\" + json.dumps(chart_data()) + \"\\n```\\n\"))\n    assert \"<figure\" not in html and \"<code\" in html\n\n\ndef test_the_same_body_renders_the_same_bytes_and_another_body_another_id():\n    body = fence(json.dumps(chart_data()))\n    assert str(render_markdown(body)) == str(render_markdown(body))\n    ids = {re.search(r'id=\"([^\"]+)\"', str(render_markdown(text)))[1]\n           for text in (body, body + \"\\nMore.\\n\")}\n    assert len(ids) == 2\n\n\n# Drawing.\n\ndef numbers(figure: Figure, tag: str, attribute: str) -> list[float]:\n    values = []\n    index = 0\n    for element in figure.elements:\n        own = {}\n        while index < len(figure.attributes) and figure.attributes[index][0] == element and (\n                figure.attributes[index][1] not in own):\n            own[figure.attributes[index][1]] = figure.attributes[index][2]\n            index += 1\n        if element == tag and attribute in own:\n            values.append(float(own[attribute]))\n    return values\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind\", [\"bar\", \"hbar\"])\ndef test_a_bar_chart_starts_at_zero(kind):\n    html = drawn(type=kind, series=[series(\"900\", \"950\")])\n    ticks = re.findall(r'class=\"chart-tick\"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', html)\n    assert ticks[0] == \"0\"\n    baseline = re.search(r'class=\"chart-baseline\" x1=\"([\\d.]+)\" y1=\"([\\d.]+)\"', html)\n    rects = re.findall(r'<rect class=\"chart-series-1\" x=\"([\\d.]+)\" y=\"([\\d.]+)\" width=\"([\\d.]+)\"'\n                       r' height=\"([\\d.]+)\"', html)\n    for x, y, width, height in rects:\n        if kind == \"bar\":\n            assert float(y) + float(height) == pytest.approx(float(baseline[2]))\n        else:\n            assert float(x) == pytest.approx(float(baseline[1]))\n    assert \"not zero\" not in html\n\n\ndef test_a_bar_chart_with_negatives_spans_zero_with_bars_either_side():\n    html = drawn(series=[series(\"-50\", \"100\")])\n    ticks = re.findall(r'class=\"chart-tick\"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', html)\n    assert ticks[0].startswith(\"-\") and \"0\" in ticks\n\n\ndef test_a_line_chart_above_zero_says_where_it_starts():\n    html = drawn(type=\"line\", series=[series(\"900\", \"950\")],\n                 unit={\"text\": \"$\", \"position\": \"prefix\"})\n    assert '<p class=\"chart-note\"><small>The vertical axis starts at $890, not zero.</small></p>' in html\n\n\ndef test_a_line_chart_near_zero_starts_at_zero_and_says_nothing():\n    html = drawn(type=\"line\", series=[series(\"10\", \"100\")])\n    assert re.findall(r'class=\"chart-tick\"[^>]*>([^<]*)<', html)[0] == \"0\"\n    assert \"not zero\" not in html\n\n\ndef values[10:13] = [\"\", \"7\", \"\"]\n    html = drawn(type=\"line\", categories=[str(i) for i in range(30)], series=[series(*values)])\n    assert html.count(\"<circle\") == 1\n\n\ndef                series=[series(\"1,200\", \"$4.50\", \"(3.2)\", \"<10\", \"n/a\", \"—\", \"\")],\n                 unit={\"text\": \"$\", \"position\": \"prefix\"})\n    table =   assert TITLE_ID.fullmatch(title_id)\n    assert f'role=\"img\" aria-labelledby=\"{title_id}\"' in html\n\n\ndef test_the_drawing_refuses_anything_outside_its_vocabulary():\n    with {"parentUuid":"f5227b80-a8e9-4ee4-a851-a50c50fa6956","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbfKzooBquCh6Zvym9LW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TRG1mD8RhkeadPA51wRzpr","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"uv run pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -1 && git add app/chart_drawing.py app/rendering.py app/public_site.py docs/adr/ADR-006-charts-drawn-from-data.md tests/test_t16_chart_rendering.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT16: draw Charts as inline SVG behind the trusted boundary\n\napp.chart_drawing draws a parsed Chart: vertical bar, horizontal bar, and\nline, 1 to 4 series with a legend for two or more, the fixed palette (its\ndark steps by class), a zero baseline for bars, a note when a line starts\nabove zero, and no mark for a missing or suppressed value (a line gaps).\nUnder it go the privacy note once, the source, and a \"Show the data\" table\nin the original notation. {"parentUuid":"3b13cc80-15b9-4521-9ab1-8911bbee2ae3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfbh1W68MvXe6midVRFk3","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019BaTM2VBvXMrhZCVtQ7Yxy","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437/scratchpad && cat > $S/t16-review.md <<'EOF'\n## `/code-review` findings (7031100..494fc38)\n\nTen findings. The fixes are in 1729d52, with tests that fail on the code before it (8 of the 9 new ones; the 9th is an all-positive control).\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | A negative bar's value label on a horizontal bar chart is drawn over the category names and past the SVG's left edge | **Fixed.** The layout leaves room for negative values' labels between the category names and the plot. Tested for each drawing (`-10`, `-1,000.5`) |\n| 2 | A negative bar's value label on a vertical bar chart lands on the category labels | **Fixed.** Room for it is left below the plot when a labelled bar is negative, and the category labels move down |\n| 3 | A label above a bar that reaches the top tick (`100`, `50`) is clipped at the top of the SVG | **Fixed.** Room for the labels is left above the plot whenever bars are labelled |\n| 4 | A stored invalid Chart blocks every save of its item, and the writer can't see its source to fix it | **Kept.** Spec #14 refuses a body with an invalid Chart on every save path. No stored body has a `chart` fence, and the locked block's **Remove** button lets a writer save. T17's builder should open a stored invalid Chart so it can be fixed in place: noted for T17 |\n| 5 | A word unit (`tonnes`) is shown nowhere when there's a y label | **Fixed.** It goes beside the value axis label: \"Exports (tonnes)\" |\n| 6 | A Chart inside a list or quote isn't put in canonical form, against ADR-006's wording | **ADR clarified.** Only a top-level Chart is rewritten. Rewriting a nested one would mean rewriting the list's or quote's own markers. It is still checked and drawn |\n| 7 | Error messages call `x_label` \"the horizontal axis label\", which is wrong for a horizontal bar chart | **Fixed.** Errors say \"the category axis label\" and \"the value axis label\" |\n| 8 | No 768 or 1440 px screenshots (global CLAUDE.md) | **Noted, not done.** The browser automation here can't set the viewport to those widths (see the browser check). From about 704 px up, the content column caps a Chart at 672 px, so 768 and 1440 draw as at 1200 |\n| 9 | Cleanup: an unused `PREFIX` import, the two layouts repeat their axis setup, and `effective_unit` is computed about 8 times per drawing | **Fixed.** The import is gone, a shared `_axis`, and `effective_unit` is a `cached_property` |\n| 10 | A fallback save parses the body and each Chart twice: once to canonicalize, once to validate | **Kept.** It costs little against a 32 KB cap, and keeping `content.validate` as the one gate every save path goes through is worth more |\n\n`uv run pytest`: 1063 passed.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 19 --body-file $S/t16-review.md","description":"Post the review findings on issue 19"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":741,"cache_read_input_tokens":323435,"output_tokens":1290,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":61},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":741,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1290,"cache_read_input_tokens":323435,"cache_creation_input_tokens":741,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":741},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_019BaTM2VBvXMrhZCVtQ7Yxy":{"command":"cd /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437/scratchpad && cat > $S/t16-review.md <<'EOF'\n## `/code-review` findings (7031100..494fc38)\n\nTen findings. Two Data Bites were stored there and published: \"Chart check\" (a bar Chart with `<10`, a 4-series horizontal bar Chart with `n/a` and `*`, and an 11-year line Chart with `—`), and \"Negative check\" (negative values on both bar types).\n\n| Check | Actions | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Bar** | Open the public page | **Pass.** It starts at zero. Values are labelled as typed (`482`), `<10` is labelled with no bar, and the source line and the privacy note sit under it. `docs/screenshots/charts-bar-desktop-1200.jpg` |\n| **Horizontal bar, 4 series** | Scroll to it | **Pass.** There's a legend for the four series. `n/a` and `*` draw no bar, and the privacy note appears once. `charts-hbar-desktop-1200.jpg` |\n| **Line** | Scroll to it | **Pass.** It has a gap at 2019 (`—`), markers with a surface ring, an end label as typed (`92`), and \"The vertical axis starts at 88%, not zero.\" under it |\n| **Show the data** | Open each `<details>` | **Pass.** The table keeps the original notation (`—`, `<10`), right-aligned. `charts-line-and-data-desktop-1200.jpg` |\n| **Editor** | Open the item's edit page | **Pass.** Each Chart is a locked block, drawn, with **Remove**, and its JSON is nowhere in the page. `charts-editor-and-phone-preview.jpg` |\n| **Phone** (before) | Press **Phone** in the Site preview | **Fail, then fixed.** One drawing scaled to 356 px put Chart text near 9 px. `charts-phone-390-before.png`. Fixed in 494fc38 with a second, 360-unit drawing shown below 30rem |\n| **Phone** (after) | Reload and press **Phone** | **Pass.** Only the phone drawings show, with text about 13 px and no sideways page scroll. The line Chart labels every second year, and long category names are shortened. `charts-phone-390-bar.png`, `charts-phone-390-hbar.png`, `charts-phone-390-line.png` |\n| **Desktop** after the fix | Open the public page at 1200 px | **Pass.** Only the wide drawings show, and the page is 1200 px wide with no sideways scroll |\n| **Negative values** (after the review fixes) | Open \"Negative check\" | **Pass.** `100` at the top tick isn't clipped. `-10` and `-3` sit below their bars and above the category labels. `-1,000.5` sits between the category names and its bar. A word unit reads \"Exports (students)\". `charts-negative-labels-1200.jpg` |\n| Console | | **Pass.** No errors |\n\n**Not done:**\n- **Safari.**\n- **Dark mode.** Chrome's colour scheme couldn't be switched from the automation. The dark palette passed the dataviz validator against `#121212`, but it wasn't seen on screen.\n- **768 and 1440 viewports.** The automation's window resize doesn't change the viewport. {"parentUuid":"e6cc049c-9cd9-4bf4-9970-1852b74f70d8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfbh52uNBNAV41iLDk6kW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SKtP6U3FD86uuknzsnWZec","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/.claude/projects/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/memory/browser-checks-environment.md","content":"---\nname: browser-checks-environment\ndescription: What works for ticket browser checks here: viewport widths, phone width, real pastes, scratch instance\nmetadata:\n  type: reference\n---\n\nBrowser checks for closing comments (spec #14) in this environment, as of 2026-10-01:\n\n- **Claude in Chrome's resize_window doesn't change the viewport** (stayed 516 px, or whatever the window is). 768/1440 px checks can't be done that way.\n- **gstack `browse` (headless) is killed by the command sandbox** (exit 137), and running it with the sandbox disabled was refused by the auto-mode classifier.
